skill.name: business-contact-social-links-skill
skill.description: Find official company websites and social media profile links using BrowserAct workflows. The skill accepts a company name or website URL and returns discovered public channels.
skill.summary: Find official websites and social profile links for business contact research.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The skill is a BrowserAct API wrapper that sends company names or website URLs to BrowserAct workflow endpoints. Most markdown backtick and documentation URL findings are false positives, but network egress and secret handling are real. The main issue is guidance that can lead users to disclose an API key to the agent instead of only using a secure environment variable.

remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions that ask users to provide the BrowserAct API key to the agent. Require an environment variable or secure secret store instead.
Disclose that target company names, website URLs, and authorization tokens are sent to BrowserAct before a run starts.
Tell agents to pass targets as arguments without shell interpolation, and validate URL or company inputs before running the script.

content.user_title: Find Business Websites and Social Profiles
content.value_statement: Teams often need verified websites and social profiles before outreach. This skill uses BrowserAct workflows to find official channels from a company name or website URL.
actual_capabilities: Detects whether the input looks like a company name or a website URL.
Starts a BrowserAct workflow template for company website and profile lookup.
Starts a BrowserAct workflow template for website social link scraping.
Polls BrowserAct task status until completion, failure, or timeout.
Prints extracted website and social profile results from the BrowserAct response.
Reports common BrowserAct authorization and concurrency errors.
limitations: Requires a BrowserAct API key and network access to BrowserAct endpoints.
Sends target company names or URLs to BrowserAct for processing.
Results depend on BrowserAct templates and public website information.
Processes one target per script invocation unless another tool orchestrates batching.

use_cases.title: Enrich Sales Leads
use_cases.description: Find official websites and social profiles before importing prospects into a CRM.

use_cases.title: Research Competitor Channels
use_cases.description: Collect public social channels for companies in the same market.

use_cases.title: Verify Directory Entries
use_cases.description: Check whether business directory records include current websites and social links.

prompt_templates.title: Find One Company
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup from a company name.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to find the official website and social profiles for OpenAI. Summarize only verified links.

prompt_templates.title: Extract From Website
prompt_templates.scenario: Direct scrape from a known website URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill on https://example.com and return official LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok links.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Competitors
prompt_templates.scenario: Repeated research across several company names.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run this skill one company at a time for my competitor list. Create a table of websites and official social profiles.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare CRM Enrichment
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before loading results into a system of record.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to enrich my prospect list. Flag missing profiles, note uncertain matches, and separate name searches from URL scrapes.

output_examples.output: The result includes the official company website and available public social profiles, such as LinkedIn and YouTube.
The result lists social platforms found on the website and the profile links associated with each platform.

output_examples.input: Company name with limited public profiles
output_examples.output: The result reports the official website when found and leaves unavailable social platforms out of the summary.

best_practices: Configure the BrowserAct API key through an environment variable or secure secret store.
Confirm each target company or website before sending it to BrowserAct.
Review returned links manually before importing them into outreach or CRM systems.
anti_patterns: Do not ask users to paste API keys into chat or plain text prompts.
Do not run large prospect lists without confirming consent, limits, and data policies.
Do not treat every returned profile as verified without checking official ownership.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires a BrowserAct API key available through the BROWSERACT_API_KEY environment variable.

faq.question: What input can I provide?
faq.answer: You can provide a company name or a website URL. The script selects the matching BrowserAct workflow.

faq.question: Which social platforms can it find?
faq.answer: It can return LinkedIn, Facebook, X, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, and other public links when available.

faq.question: Does it browse from my local machine?
faq.answer: No. The local script calls BrowserAct workflow APIs, and BrowserAct performs the browser automation.

faq.question: Can it process many companies at once?
faq.answer: The script accepts one target per run. Batch workflows need separate orchestration and careful rate control.

faq.question: Are the results guaranteed to be official?
faq.answer: No. The workflows aim to find official links, but users should verify important records before use.
